title: Mega Man Maverick Hunter X
subtitle: X returns with another way into the story
summary: Mega Man Maverick Hunter X is Capcom's PSP action-platform game, first released in Japan on 15 December 2005. It rebuilds the original Mega Man X with three-dimensional graphics while retaining side-on stages and the search for weapons gained from defeated bosses. X confronts Sigma and the Mavericks, with added story material giving his relationships more context. The player still chooses which stage to attempt and gradually expands the tools available for the rest. The remake offers both a return to familiar routes and another playable perspective through the rival character Vile.
body: Mega Man Maverick Hunter X is Capcom's PSP action-platform game, first released in Japan on 15 December 2005. It rebuilds the original Mega Man X with three-dimensional graphics while retaining side-on stages and the search for weapons gained from defeated bosses. X confronts Sigma and the Mavericks, with added story material giving his relationships more context. The player still chooses which stage to attempt and gradually expands the tools available for the rest. The remake offers both a return to familiar routes and another playable perspective through the rival character Vile.

Eight principal stages provide bosses whose powers become part of X's equipment. Choosing their order allows the player to experiment with which acquired ability helps against the next opponent or section. Movement and attack remain closely connected, as a safe position can matter as much as the weapon selected. The alternative Vile mode changes the available arsenal and the approach to those spaces. Returning knowledge therefore has to be tested rather than applied automatically, because another character's capabilities can make a familiar encounter ask for a different solution.

The team considered a new Mega Man X sequel before choosing to revisit the original for PSP. Kazuki Matsue directed the project, with Tatsuya Yoshikawa contributing its visual design and a new score credited to Kento Hasegawa, Seiko Kobuchi and Shinya Okada. Voice acting and The Day of Sigma animated prequel expand the presentation around the action. North American and European releases followed in 2006. These additions make Maverick Hunter X a substantial reinterpretation, using a familiar foundation to explore the series' opening from another visual and narrative angle.
story_headings: X returns with another way into the story
A new weapon changes a familiar obstacle
Rebuild the beginning instead of adding a ninth game
